_requireApprovingReview: FALSE on an explicit decision (2026-08-31): the agent merges to main on green CI alone. Name it for what it is — a WEAKER bar than requiring a review, because nothing reads the diff but the test suite — and a bar the OTHER operator also lives under, since main is shared. What keeps it defensible: every workflow runs on every PR (ciPaths is '**', so a vacuous green cannot occur), the hardStop list below fences the security boundaries however green, and per AGENTS.md invariant 5 nothing on main reaches anyone's hardware until that machine's owner bumps their SHA pin. The pin is the real gate.
_requireApprovingReview_flipBack: Set this back to TRUE the moment the ai-review reviewer starts posting on this repo. The reviewer is this repo's own services/github-review, but its registry (agent-review.yml) is per-operator and private, so the entry cannot live here. And it can ONLY reach this repo through its poll backstop: this repo is PUBLIC, a public repo cannot call a private reusable workflow, and GitHub resolves the callee before any job-level `if` — such a job fails the whole workflow to load with zero jobs (seen 2026-08-22, cultuvilla run 32594475090). Do not add a request-review job to .github/workflows/. The cost of the backstop is latency, not capability.
_reviewTimeoutMs: Only consulted while requireApprovingReview is true; kept short so the flip back does not also mean a long idle.
_mergeMethod: Every PR landed here so far is one commit on main with no merge commit (#1–#6); the six merge commits in history predate the extraction. Squash keeps that.
_ciPaths: No workflow under .github/workflows/ carries a paths: filter — every push and PR to main runs all five (ansible, gitleaks, mypy, pytest, ruff). '**' says that directly; enumerating directories would silently stop being true the moment one is added.
_requiredLanes: Checks that must reach SUCCESS on every PR — SKIPPED counts as FAILED. Only unconditional jobs may be listed, matched exactly on the display name `gh pr checks` reports. The pytest and mypy matrices both name their jobs `ci-controller` / `github-review`, so those names are ambiguous and are deliberately absent; they are still gated as ordinary checks.
_sharedBlastRadius: A base move here forces a rebase even with no direct file overlap: the root tooling config every service lints against, and the lockfiles.
_hardStop: Never self-merges, however green. These are the paths where 'the tests passed' and 'the blast radius is acceptable' are different questions — each is a security or trust boundary that a test suite cannot judge. This is the ENFORCED half of the Autonomy contract in AGENTS.md; pr:land regexes changed file paths against these and nothing else. The credential line between dispatcher and scheduler is NOT a path and cannot be listed — that half is agent discipline, stated in AGENTS.md.

hardStop.why: the CI fabric's only access control (ADR 0026)
exposes a Docker socket on a machine someone else owns
the boundary untrusted job code runs inside
invariant 4's tripwire — weakening it is a placement decision, not a test edit
